capitals.name: Lakeba (Lau)
capitals.note: The Tovata page gives no capital; the Ma'afu page says he 'established himself at Lakeba' in 1848 and later took up residence in Lomaloma. Coordinates approximate.

rulers.name: Enele Ma'afu (Tui Lau)
rulers.title: Tui Lau (King of Lau)
rulers.note: Conceived the confederacy 'on 14 February 1867' (Tovata page); granted the title Tui Lau by the Lauan chiefs in February 1869 (Ma'afu page). The Tovata page says there was no paramount chief: the four chiefs were Tui Bua, Tui Cakau, Tui Lau and Tui Macuata.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Ma'afu's base: Lakeba and the Lau Islands from 1848, Vanua Balavu in 1850 (Ma'afu page). The Tovata page names Bua, Macuata and Cakaudrove as members but dates no joining; the Ma'afu page has the Cakaudrove and Bua chiefs recognising him only in May 1869. The Lau radius is a coordinate stand-in (gazetteer_names_needed: Lau Islands).

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'Location: North-east Fiji: Bua, Macuata, and Cakaudrove on Vanua Levu, plus the Lau Islands' (Tovata infobox). Macuata's date is not on any page opened and is placed with Cakaudrove and Bua in 1869 at low confidence. No area given on either page.

ledger.note: 1867: Ma'afu conceives the Tovata Confederacy. 'was conceived on 14 February 1867 by the Tui Lau, Ma'afu'; Ma'afu page: 'In 1867, he created the Tovata Confederacy'. The Tovata page names Bua, Macuata, Cakaudrove and Lau as its area but not when each joined, so the dossier starts on the Lau core.

region.text: Bua, Cakaudrove and Macuata on Vanua Levu (and Taveuni)

ledger.note: 1869: the northern chiefs recognise Ma'afu. 'Lauan chiefs met in Lakeba and February 1869, and granted Ma'afu the title of' Tui Lau; the Cakaudrove and Bua chiefs later recognised him 'in May 1869'. Macuata is the researcher's reading: the Tovata page lists it as a member, undated.

ledger.note: 1871: the confederacy comes under the Fijian crown. Bridging event, as in the Kingdom of Fiji dossier: no page opened dates Ma'afu's adhesion; the Kingdom of Fiji page says the kingdom 'covered all of modern Fiji, except the island of Rotuma' and calls Ma'afu Cakobau's 'old rival' who signed the 10 October 1874 Deed of Cession, but is silent on whether or when he joined (Cakobau was regarded by other chiefs as 'first among equals'); Ma'afu page: he 'played a leading role in the cession of Fiji to the United Kingdom in 1874'.

certainty.note: A confederacy of chiefdoms with no paramount chief; island coasts exact.

sources.title: Tovata
sources.note: Conceived 14 February 1867 by Ma'afu; members Lau, Cakaudrove, Bua, Macuata; no capital, no other dates.

sources.title: Enele Maʻafu
sources.note: Lakeba 1848; Tui Lau February 1869; Cakaudrove and Bua May 1869; 1874 cession; death 6 February 1881.

sources.title: Seru Epenisa Cakobau
sources.note: Silent on Tovata; used for the relation to Cakobau (1865-1871).

sources.title: Kingdom of Fiji
sources.note: Opened for the 1871 merge: kingdom 'covered all of modern Fiji, except the island of Rotuma'; silent on Ma'afu's adhesion and does not mention Tovata, so the event is confidence 1.

notes: A state Cliopatria lacks; named as a predecessor by kingdom-of-fiji. The only Tovata page is a stub (conception date, member provinces, no history): founding 1867 is the conception date, the Lau/Cakaudrove/Bua recognitions are 1869, and Macuata and the 1871 adhesion are bridged. The 1871 event rests on the Kingdom of Fiji page, which is silent on Ma'afu's adhesion (confidence 1, a gap for the reviewer). Not on any page opened: Ma'afu's conquests (Moala, Ritova, Macuata, Bua), the Confederacy of Independent Kingdoms of Viti (1865-1867, Ma'afu's relation to it), the 1872-1874 vacillation between Cakobau and Ma'afu, a capital. The Tovata page says the confederacy was headed by the British consul at Levuka as 'prime minister'. Region names: the Lau radius is a coordinate stand-in (gazetteer_names_needed: Lau Islands, Vanua Levu as regions).
